_readme: WHICH EXAMPLES ARE SWEPT OVER EVERY RUNNABLE SOLVER METHOD -- the selection,
as DATA. `gen_baselines.py --methods` reads this file and nothing else to
decide what to golden, so asking for more (or less) coverage is an edit here
and not an edit to the generator.
WHY A SUBSET. The 209 baselines already cover breadth of MODELS; what they do
not cover is breadth of METHODS, because a `solvers` key of `MVA` means that
family's DEFAULT path and nothing else. `model.findSolver()` reports on the
order of a hundred runnable (family, method) pairs per model, so sweeping the
whole corpus is ~25,000 solves per codebase per run. The examples below are
chosen instead to span the model SHAPES that make methods behave differently:
a method that is wrong is wrong on a shape, not on an example.
HOW MUCH THIS IS, measured with `example_methods.py --runnable` on 2026-09-04:
the fifteen examples below report 1121 runnable pairs, 1022 after
`excludeFamilies` (828 deterministic, 194 simulation-class), which is about
9,200 solves for a generation run across the nine rows. Widest is
cqn_repairmen at 140 pairs over nine families; narrowest is lqn_twotasks at
10, where only `ln` and `ldes` accept a layered model. Fewer will be WRITTEN:
the gate quarantines every pair the rows disagree on.
WHAT IS GOLDENED. For each example here, every pair `findSolver()` marks
Runnable, keyed `FAMILY:method` beside the existing bare `FAMILY` key. The
bare key keeps its exact meaning -- the family's default path as the example
itself drove it -- so nothing below changes an existing baseline. The gate is
unchanged too: a swept method whose rows disagreed is quarantined and printed,
never written with inflated slack. See README.md, `The one rule`.
THE RUNNABLE SET IS ENUMERATED ONCE, from native Python's `findSolver()` on
the model the example builds, and the SAME list is then asked of every row.
Letting each codebase enumerate its own would make the rows structurally
incomparable -- a pair one codebase never ran is not a disagreement -- and it
is the same reason the `--method` an example pins is read once and passed to
both CLIs (see parity-static/runner.py).
`simulationDefaults` is the seed and run length EVERY row gives a pair whose
findSolver Class is `simulation`. Left to each engine's own default the four
codebases walk four different sample paths, which is not a disagreement about
the model and would quarantine most simulated pairs for a reason that says
nothing about either codebase. Removing the block is allowed and simply
returns those pairs to the engines' defaults; it does not loosen a tolerance.
`excludeFamilies` and `excludeMethods` are the pairs the sweep never ASKS for,
each with the reason. They are not tolerance grants: a pair listed here is not
goldened at all, rather than goldened with slack. `auto` is NOT among them and
cannot be: AUTO is the vehicle the sweep asks a pair through
(`SolverAUTO(model, 'mva.schmidt')`) and is not itself a family findSolver
reports, so there is nothing to exclude -- no swept table is ever keyed AUTO.

examples.why: The smallest model in the corpus and the only shape where a wrong method is unambiguously wrong: the exact answer is closed form, so a method that disagrees disagrees with arithmetic, not with another approximation.

examples.shape: open, two classes, PS queues plus an INF delay
examples.why: The open arm with several classes: everything that closes an open chain -- the MAM decompositions, NC's open terms, the AMVA arrival theorems -- runs here with no closed population in the way.

examples.shape: closed, single class, delay plus queue
examples.why: Closed single class, where every population recursion (comom, cub, rgf, gm, pana, ...) collapses to one chain, so a normalizing-constant method that mishandles the one-chain case has nowhere to hide. Its golden already carries seven families, the widest in the corpus.

examples.shape: closed, two classes, PS queues plus an INF delay
examples.why: The closed multiclass shape the AMVA family is written for, and the shape whose defect motivated this coverage: the native-Python closed-population AMVA arm returned [2, 0] where the answer is [1.4118, 0.5882].

examples.shape: mixed, one open and one closed class, PS, Erlang/HyperExp
examples.why: The one shape where a method must combine an open and a closed chain in the SAME fixed point. Several AMVA and NC arms treat the mixture differently, and no bare-family golden separates them.

examples.shape: closed, four classes, multiserver FCFS, a Disabled station-class pair
examples.why: Multiserver: every multiserver correction (the multiserver rules, NC's load-dependent arms, the QBD folding) is a distinct code path from the single-server one, and a Disabled pair checks that the sweep does not fabricate a row the model refuses.

examples.shape: closed, three chains over five classes with class switching, FCFS and PS, product form
examples.why: Class switching into SEVERAL chains, which is the construction the native-Python AMVA defect corrupted; five classes over three chains is where a method that folds the chains wrongly cannot land on the right answer by symmetry. Preferred over cqn_twoclass_erl, whose WRROBIN routing leaves only simulators runnable (17 pairs, all stochastic) -- and a golden holding only stochastic keys cannot fail a run.

examples.shape: class switching by routing, diamond topology
examples.why: Class switching by ROUTING rather than by a ClassSwitch node -- a different chain construction from cqn_twoclass_erl, and the one a method is more likely to get right by accident on a two-station model.

The cache arms of NC and the RMF/fluid cache methods answer a different question from the queueing arms of the same families, and no bare-family golden reaches them: a cache method is compared nowhere else per method.

The fork-join transformation runs BEFORE the solver, so every method is asked about a model the example did not build. A method that is correct on the original network can still be wrong on the transformed one.

Finite capacity: a method that ignores the buffer returns the infinite-buffer answer, which is close enough to read as correct and is not. The drop rule also gives the sweep a loss metric to disagree about.
Load dependence: the LD arms of MVA and NC are separate implementations from the load-independent ones, reached only by a model that declares a rate function.

Priority: only some methods carry priority at all, and the ones that do are the methods that disagree most. A family default that handles priority says nothing about the fifteen other tokens of that family.
An SPN reaches the solvers through a different model translation, so a method's SPN arm is not its queueing arm and is not covered by any queueing example here.

Layered: an `ln.*` method is a LAYERING STRATEGY (srvn, flat, ph, cs, moment3) -- how the model is cut into layers, not which solver runs them -- and no bare-family golden distinguishes two cuts of the same model. It is also where the sweep's reach differs most across codebases: line-cli takes only default/moment3/mwba.* as --method on the layered path, so the strategy tokens are a MATLAB and Python capability the C++ row reports by name.

excludeFamilies.why: QNS is a meta-solver over the external qnsolver binary, and is already in gen_baselines.META_SOLVERS.

The lqns/lqsim binaries are third-party, at a version this repository does not track, so their numbers are not evidence about this codebase. runner.JAVA_PORTED_SOLVERS already declines to drive them for that reason.
